summary: Brazil voted on Oct 4 and the result surprised markets. Flavio Bolsonaro took about 47% of valid votes to Lula's about 45%, so the two meet in a runoff on Oct 25. Investors read his lead as a sign of spending cuts and reform, and Brazilian stocks and the real jumped: the Ibovespa rose 7.7% on Oct 5 and hit a new record of 209,067 on Oct 9, with the real near 5.00 per dollar. The central bank cut the Selic to 13.75% on Sep 16, but September inflation came in at 4.58% over 12 months, above the 4.5% ceiling, which limits more cuts. The rally has priced in a Bolsonaro win (prediction markets near 87% to 89% on Oct 10), so a Lula comeback on Oct 25 is the main risk, and a 25% US Section 301 tariff on many Brazilian goods (since Jul 22) still hangs over exporters and the Pix payment system. The runoff has tightened: Quaest (Oct 14) and Datafolha (Oct 15, per O Povo) both show 51% to 49% for Flavio Bolsonaro, inside the margin of error. A Vox Brasil poll taken Oct 15 to 17 is the first recent poll with Lula ahead, 51% to 49% of valid votes. New polls on Oct 20 mostly lean to Bolsonaro: Real Time Big Data has 52% to 48% and Gerp 53% to 47%, while Data Ranking has Lula 50.4% to 49.6%. The Ibovespa rose 1.57% to 208,295.98 on Oct 20 and the real firmed to about 5.02. Quaest's Oct 21 poll has Flavio Bolsonaro at 45% and Lula at 44%, down from 46% to 44% a week earlier, so the race is within one point. The final polls before Sunday's runoff show a tie: Datafolha 50% to 50% of valid votes and PoderData 51% to 49% for Flavio Bolsonaro, both released Oct 22.
for_you: The Oct 25 runoff is close to a coin flip. NU is 'Buy zone now' (14.56 on Oct 16, zone 14.03 to 15.08), but wait until after the vote before buying or selling puts on Brazil names: a Lula win could knock Brazilian banks 5% to 10% in a day. The BBD insider cluster (22 insiders, about $100 million, last buys Sep 28) still stands. MELI is rated Avoid.

watch.name: Real per US dollar
watch.why: Firmed about 0.6% on Oct 20 on the runoff poll (Closing Look). A stronger real lifts the dollar value of every Brazilian stock.

watch.name: Selic policy rate
watch.why: Cut by 0.25 point on Sep 16. Next decision Nov 3 to 4. Lower rates help banks' credit quality, retailers and fintech lenders.

watch.name: Ibovespa
watch.why: Up 1.57% on the runoff trade, just under the 209,067 record of Oct 9.

watch.name: Presidential runoff
watch.why: Flavio Bolsonaro vs Lula on Sunday. Final polls are a tie: Datafolha 50% to 50% of valid votes (Oct 22), PoderData 51% to 49% for Flavio (Oct 22), Quaest 45% to 44% for Flavio (Oct 21).

watch.name: IPCA inflation, 12 months
watch.why: September reading, above the 4.5% ceiling of the target range. Makes fast Selic cuts less likely.

exposed.name: MercadoLibre
exposed.exposure: about 53% of 2025 net revenue from Brazil ($15.2 billion of $28.9 billion, FY2025 10-K segment data)
exposed.how: A stronger real and lower Brazilian rates lift its reported sales and its Mercado Pago lending, and the stock rose about 9% on Oct 5.

exposed.name: Nu Holdings
exposed.exposure: most revenue and customers in Brazil, with smaller Mexico and Colombia units (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: A Brazilian digital bank, so a stronger real and hopes for lower rates help it, and it jumped about 12% to 14% on Oct 5.

exposed.name: Itau Unibanco
exposed.exposure: Brazil's largest private bank, most earnings from Brazil (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Banks move with Brazil's fiscal outlook and the real, and the ADR rose about 15% on Oct 5.

exposed.name: Banco Bradesco
exposed.exposure: nearly all business in Brazil (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: The ADR rose about 19% on Oct 5 as investors bet on spending cuts and lower rates.

exposed.name: Petrobras
exposed.exposure: state controlled oil company, nearly all production in Brazil (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Investors expect less political meddling under Bolsonaro, but he has floated reviewing and selling Petrobras assets, so dividend and policy questions remain; ADRs rose about 8% to 12% on Oct 5.

exposed.name: Vale
exposed.exposure: Brazil based iron ore miner, mines mostly in Brazil, sales mostly to China (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Rallied with Brazilian assets after the vote, but its earnings depend more on iron ore prices and China than on Brasilia.

exposed.name: XP Inc
exposed.exposure: Brazilian broker and investment platform, nearly all revenue in Brazil (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: A local stock rally and falling rates bring more trading and more money moving from fixed income into stocks.

exposed.name: StoneCo
exposed.exposure: Brazilian card acquirer and small business bank, nearly all revenue in Brazil (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Lower funding costs help its card prepayment business, but Pix, the free central bank payment system, keeps eating into card fees.

exposed.name: PagSeguro
exposed.exposure: Brazilian payments company, nearly all revenue in Brazil (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Same as StoneCo: helped by lower rates and a stronger real, squeezed by Pix.

exposed.name: Sabesp
exposed.exposure: Sao Paulo water and sewage utility, all revenue in Brazil (company filings)
exposed.how: A privatized utility that benefits when long term Brazilian interest rates fall and the political mood favors private capital.

exposed.name: Embraer
exposed.exposure: Brazil based plane maker, large share of sales to US airlines (company filings, approximate)
exposed.how: Aircraft and parts were carved out of the 25% US Section 301 tariff, so trade news matters more than the election; a stronger real raises its Brazilian costs.

changes.what: Brazil's central bank cut the Selic by 0.25 point to 13.75% in a unanimous vote, its first cut right before an election in two decades. Lower rates help banks, lenders and retailers.
First round vote: Flavio Bolsonaro 47% to Lula 45%, against polls that had Lula ahead. Runoff set for Oct 25.
Brazilian assets rallied on the result. Ibovespa up 7.7% to a record 206,912, the real up about 4% to 5.00 per dollar, Bradesco ADR up about 19%, Itau about 15%, Nu about 12%, MercadoLibre about 9%.
September inflation came in at 0.82% for the month and 4.58% over 12 months, above the 4.5% ceiling. The Ibovespa still closed at a new record of 209,067 as runoff polls favored Bolsonaro.

AtlasIntel's runoff poll for Bloomberg (Oct 3 to 8, 5,026 people, released Oct 9) gives Flavio Bolsonaro 52.8% of valid votes to Lula's 47.2%, wider than Datafolha's 52% to 48%. Bolsonaro rose from 47.4% to 51.1% of total votes since Atlas's last poll, breaking the earlier tie.
changes.for_you: Markets already price a Bolsonaro win, so the poll mostly lowers the odds of a shock. Still no new Brazil swings or puts into the Oct 25 runoff. PBR is left out of both lists: a new government could change its pricing policy either way.

changes.what: The runoff is tightening. Quaest (Oct 10 to 13, 2,154 people, released Oct 14) has Flavio Bolsonaro at 51% of valid votes to Lula's 49%, and O Povo reports Datafolha (Oct 13 to 15) at the same 51% to 49%, down from 52% to 48% earlier and inside the 2 point margin of error. EWZ fell 2.4% to 41.58 on Oct 15.
changes.for_you: Brazilian banks rallied on a Bolsonaro lead that is now inside the margin of error. NU is 'Buy zone now', but wait for the Oct 25 result before acting.

changes.what: A Futura/100% Cidades poll released Oct 16 has Flavio Bolsonaro at 50.8% of valid votes to Lula's 49.2%, a technical tie inside its 2.2 point margin. An average of eleven pollsters is 51.6% to 48.4%, with nine showing Bolsonaro ahead, while Polymarket (77%) and Kalshi (78%) gave Bolsonaro much higher odds as of Oct 16 (Rio Times). EWZ rose 0.6% to 41.83 on 1.58x volume and NU fell 1.2% to 14.56 (dashboard).
changes.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. Betting markets are far more confident than the polls, so a Lula win is the bigger surprise and would likely hit NU, ITUB and BBD hardest; a Bolsonaro win is mostly priced. All are left out of both lists because the result is still a coin flip in the polls. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now' but wait for the vote.

changes.what: A Vox Brasil poll of 2,100 voters taken Oct 15 to 17 has Lula at 51% of valid votes to Flavio Bolsonaro's 49%, the first recent poll with Lula ahead (Rio Times). Datafolha (Oct 13 to 14) still has Bolsonaro 51% to 49%, and all recent polls are inside their margins of error. Betting markets were far more confident in Bolsonaro (77% to 78% on Oct 16), so the gap between polls and prices is the risk.
changes.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now', but a Lula win would likely hit NU, ITUB and BBD, while a Bolsonaro win is mostly priced. All are left out of both lists because the polls are a coin flip.

changes.what: AtlasIntel (reported Oct 19) has Flavio Bolsonaro at 49.8% to Lula's 47.6%, or 51.1% to 48.9% of valid votes, down from a 5.4 point lead on Oct 9; Nexus for BTG Pactual has 46.5% to 45.9%. Prediction markets still give Bolsonaro about 77% (Polymarket) to 80% (Kalshi), so polls are tighter than prices.
changes.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now' (zone 14.03 to 15.08), but a Lula win could hit Brazilian banks hard in a day. All four are left out of both lists while the race is this close.

changes.what: Polls published Oct 20 mostly lean to Flavio Bolsonaro: Real Time Big Data (Oct 15 to 19, 2,000 voters) has 52% to 48% of valid votes, Gerp 53% to 47%, Alfa 51.5% to 48.5% and Instituto Franca 50.8% to 49.2%, while Data Ranking has Lula 50.4% to 49.6%. The Ibovespa rose 1.57% to 208,295.98 and the real firmed to about 5.02 per dollar.
changes.for_you: No action until after Sunday's vote. NU closed 15.09 on Oct 20 (Yahoo), just above its 15.07 zone top on Oct 19 data. Markets already price a Bolsonaro win, so a Lula win is the bigger move; no Brazil puts before Monday.

changes.what: Quaest's runoff poll released Oct 21 has Flavio Bolsonaro at 45% and Lula at 44%, down from 46% to 44% on Oct 14 (Reuters). With four days to go, the race is within one point, while markets have priced a Bolsonaro win.
changes.for_you: No buys or puts on NU (15.05 on Oct 21, right at its 15.05 zone top) until after Sunday's vote. A Lula win is the bigger surprise for Brazilian banks.

changes.what: Final polls before the Oct 25 runoff show a dead heat: Datafolha has Flavio Bolsonaro and Lula at 50% each of valid votes (released Oct 22, down from 51% to 49% a week earlier), and PoderData has Flavio at 51% to 49% (released Oct 22, down from a 4 point lead). Markets have priced a Bolsonaro win, so a Lula win is the bigger surprise.
changes.for_you: No NU buys or puts before Monday. NU is 'Buy zone now' at 14.73 on Oct 22 (zone 14.11 to 15.03). If Lula wins and NU gaps toward 14.11, that is the level to watch; if Flavio wins, wait for the gap to settle.
